topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: The Nature of Cancer: Genetic Mutations, Random Chance, and Environmental Risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease and explore the interplay between intrinsic random mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis: Mutagens, Xenobiotic Metabolism, Promoters, and Host Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular, chemical, and cellular mechanisms through which pathogens, dietary toxins, radiation, chemical mutagens, non-mutagenic promoters, and host developmental stages drive cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic mutational signature, epidemiological, animal model, and in vitro testing methodologies used to identify carcinogens and determine their carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic wraps up the lecture by considering how individuals balance carcinogenic risks against practical benefits and summarizing the primary conclusions.
